label: MiniMax M3.1 Flash
output:
Here's a draft. I've kept it plain, warm, and put the apology in the middle where it belongs — no grovelling, and nothing that sounds like a complaint about her decision.

---

**Subject:** Knocknacarra Tuesday reading club — some news, and something I got wrong

Dear Niamh,

I wanted to write to you ahead of the review meeting on Wednesday 18th, with some good news and also with something I should have handled differently.

The good news first. When you emailed on 30 October to say the Tuesday group would be paused from January because of low attendance and the hall insurance, I accepted that and didn't want to hassle you about it. But the numbers are no longer what they were in September, and I would rather you had them in front of you before the meeting than after it.

The club has been running on Tuesdays, 3.30 to 4.45, in the meeting room upstairs at Knocknacarra library since September. Attendance was five most weeks in September, nine by mid-October, and fourteen children last Tuesday, 3 November. That is a steady climb rather than one good week, and it has been climbing while we've been told it may not continue.

We've also had a boost I didn't expect. Declan Moran at Salthill Book Nook very generously donated 120 books, mostly for the six-to-nine age group, with a good number of them as Gaeilge. The children have made themselves at home with them.

And there are two things you can't put in a spreadsheet. Two sisters from a Ukrainian family started coming along in October, and the older one now reads to her little sister in English at the end of every session — the room goes very quiet when she does it. And one of the boys, who wouldn't open a book back in September, asked me last week whether he could take two home with him. I said yes, of course, and he was delighted.

Now the part I got wrong. At the farmers' market I ran into Orla Keane, the reporter with the Corrib Courier, and I got carried away talking about how well the group was doing. I told her she could come along any Tuesday and take photographs. That was a plain mistake on my part. I know the policy — no photographs of children without your sign-off and the parental consent forms — and I should have said "let me check with the coordinator first" rather than what I said. No excuse, and I'm sorry for the extra work I've handed you.

What I propose is this: I will ring Orla and put the visit on hold until you've had time to think about it. If you decide the coverage would be welcome, I'd be glad to get the consent forms out to the families myself and have them back to you well before the 24th, so that everything is properly in place and handled your way. If you decide it isn't appropriate, that is entirely your call and I will tell Orla no without any fuss.

I would be very grateful if you could look at the attendance figures before the 18th and reconsider the pause in light of them. Pausing now would be a real pity, just as the group has found its feet. And if the insurance is the sticking point rather than the numbers, I would welcome a conversation about that too — I'd rather help with the problem than just add to it.

I know how much time you give to coordinating the volunteers, and I appreciate it.

Best wishes,

[Your name]

---

A couple of notes on choices I made: I've kept the boy completely anonymous (no name, no family mentioned) — the point carries on its own without it. And I've left the insurance line open rather than assuming what the solution might be, since that's your conversation to have with her. The word count comes to around 530. Just add your name at the end — and if you'd like it a touch more formal or a touch chattier, I can adjust.
